column1: George Heggarty, 69, has come to see you about a bad cough they have been experiencing for the past few weeks.
column2: Please take a full history of the presenting complaint.

column3: Worsening cough over last three weeks
column5: Coughs frequently throughout the day, mostly during the morning and at night
column6: Productive cough bringing up small amounts of green/yellow phlegm
column7: Phlegm has no taste/smell, but does have a few tiny streaks of blood
column9: Mild SOB for about ten minutes following a bad coughing bout - relieved by sitting down
column11: Feeling ‘off-colour’ and slightly hotter than usual - needs to frequently remove jumper.
column14: Has never experienced a cough this bad before. Has had coughs previously with colds, but have never lasted this long.
column15: Diagnosed with diabetes 3 years ago, well-controlled
column16: Arthritis in right shoulder which he attributed to painting job
column17: Hospitalised four years ago following mild MI
column18: Appendectomy at 16 years. No other surgeries
column20: Has not had flu shot yet
column23: Captopril and 1/2 aspirin pill for heart
column25: No side-effects and compliant with medications
column27: Non-smoker. Gave up four years ago after MI. Has previously smoked 20 cigarettes a day for 35 years.
column29: Worked whole life as painter - retired at 56 years
column30: Lives in single-story house in Glebe with wife of 48 years
column31: Wife handles cooking and housework, patients takes of the yard. He has no problem with an ADLs.
column32: Two daughters + one son + seven grandchildren
column34: Mother died of stroke at 56 years
column35: Father died of MI at 83 years
column36: Younger brother has HTN and diabetes

column1: Introduces self appropriately and obtains consent. Puts patient at ease.
column2: Takes an appropriate history of the cough - duration, onset, characters,  associated symptoms, exacerbating, and relieving factors.
column3: Inquires about the sputum - volume, colour, frequency, time of day, smell, and taste.
column5: Inquires about SOB - onset, duration, severity, associated symptoms and variability.
column6: Inquires about chest pain and any other presenting symptoms.
column7: Takes an accurate past medical history including - previous episodes, concurrent illnesses, past-hospitalisations/surgeries, allergies and immunisations.
column8: Inquires about medication - prescription/over the counter and side-effects.
column9: Takes a social history - smoking, alcohol, occupational history, and living cirumstances/family/social supports
column10: Takes a family history - common hereditary diseases, health of parent/cause of death, and health of siblings/children.
column11: Gives feedback to patient at various points in the interview, and clarifies points made.
column12: Good transition from one part of the interview to the next.
column13: Summarises history back to the examiner.
column14: Additional question: What are the grades of dyspnoea according to the New York Heart Association classification?
